A universe method, and the action internal work is held to when it
calls it.

A universe method for machines only, such as connectors delivering
messages or triggers leasing a credential. No person calls it.

A deployment method: it addresses the deployment and needs a
deployment key.

MethodGroup.description:
The methods a key may call, by group. Every public method but
`initialize` belongs to exactly one group, derived from its name, so a
new method never changes what an existing key reaches beyond its group.

oneOf.description: `session/*`, `blobs/read` and `blobs/has`.
Destructive session operations and deletion retention.

`blobs/put` alone, so connectors can upload attachments without
reading sessions.
`environments/*`, including jobs and registration keys.
Channel accounts, pairings and conversations.
`channels/inbound/admit`: what a connector delivers.
`auth/*` except leasing.
`auth/grants/lease`: resolving a brokered credential for delivery.
Environment providers and their universe bindings.
`deployment/channels/accounts/list`: a connector host's discovery.

MethodTarget.description:
Where a method names the session it acts on, so a gate can decide per
session without a hand-written table. A creation method may name one that
does not exist yet.

oneOf.description: `params.sessionId`.

parallelToolUse.description: Omitted when the provider model-list API does not report this fact.

ModelDefaultSlot.description:
A universe's model selection for a particular use. Protocol and purpose
are separate: several purposes may use the same provider API.

ModelDefaults.description:
Persisted universe defaults. Revision zero means no update has been made.
Clearing a slot still advances the revision, so setup cannot undo a clear.

expectedRevision.description:
Write only if the defaults are still at this revision, as returned by
read or put; zero for a universe with no updates. Omit it to write
whatever the current revision is.

model.description: Complete selection, or explicit null to clear this slot. Required.

headers.description:
Extra request headers sent on every request to the endpoint, alongside
the provider's own credential. Names are case-insensitive and stored
lowercased; transport headers and `authorization` are reserved.
`api-key`, `x-api-key` and `proxy-authorization` carry a secret and
accept only a `credential` value.

ModelListParams.description:
Direct provider model discovery. Results may be served from a brief
process-local cache; clients refresh by calling this method.

selectableOnly.description:
Apply Lightspeed's small, conservative selectable-model policy. It
keeps supported file-transcription routes and filters clearly unrelated
OpenAI families from agent suggestions (embeddings, moderation, image/video,
speech synthesis, and realtime). Agent suggestions also have an age limit.
Clients select routes by API kind for their intended use. This is an ID
policy, not a provider capability claim.

ModelProcessingTier.description: Provider processing class used by session defaults and per-run overrides.

oneOf.description: A universe-owned `model:<provider>` credential.
The deployment-wide fallback key from server configuration.

A credential was found and was not rejected by the provider (other
discovery errors, e.g. transport, may still be reported).
No credential anywhere: no universe row and no deployment fallback.

A credential exists but is unusable (disabled/legacy universe row) or
was rejected by the provider (HTTP 401/403).

The universe provider row explicitly configures an unauthenticated
endpoint, so no credential is expected.

ModelProviderDiscoveryView.description:
Best-effort status for one provider. A provider failure does not discard
models discovered from other providers.

credential.description:
Whether a usable credential exists for this provider — a stable signal
for clients (no string matching on `error`).

credentialSource.description: Where the credential used for this universe comes from.

error.description:
Sanitized Lightspeed error; never a credential, request header, or raw
upstream response body.

ModelView.description: A model route returned directly by a provider API.

apiKind.description: Canonical Lightspeed provider API kind, e.g. `openai:responses`.

createdAtMs.description:
Provider-reported model creation time. Omitted when the provider does
not expose one; this is distinct from the discovery fetch time.

source.description: Always `provider`; there is no maintained model catalog.

PollCursorSpec.description:
Dedupe discipline of a poll: an id set for unordered feeds, a watermark
for ordered ones.

oneOf.description: Dot path to each item's id.
Dot path to each item's monotonically increasing field.

PollCursorState.description:
Poll cursor state: Lightspeed-owned, operator-visible, reset by a spec
edit. Absent until the baseline poll.

PollHttpAuth.description:
Leased credential for an HTTP poll source; the value never appears in
the trigger document.

scheme.description: Scheme prefix; default `Bearer`, empty sends the token raw.

PollSource.description: Where a poll trigger reads from.

headers.description: Non-secret headers only; credentials come from `auth`.

environmentId.description:
Universe environment the command runs in (woken on use); absent
runs in the bot's own environment (the profile's `existing`
one), resolved at fire time.

timeoutMs.description: Job wall-clock budget; also bounds the fire activity's wait.

oneOf.description:
Borrowed CAS content: saving a profile does not retain the blob. Use
inline text, or keep this ref retained by another durable resource.

expectedRevision.description:
Checked only when the profile already exists; absent replaces (or
creates) unconditionally.

ProfileSessionRetention.description: Root-session retention policy supplied by a profile at session creation.

PromiseSourceKind.description: Where a promise's answer comes from.

RecommendedRole.description:
Universe roles as gates built on this contract name them. Core holds no
roles; this is metadata only.

RemoteMcpExecution.description:
Who connects to the server and runs its tools. `runtime`, the default, means
Lightspeed does: each call runs once, under the approval policy, and is recorded.
With `provider` the model provider does, so the endpoint must be publicly reachable
and tools run at least once: a retried generation re-sends the request, so a tool
can run again with its side effects, and the transcript shows at most one run.

RequestHeader.description:
Value of one configured request header, as an MCP server and a model
provider's endpoint both carry them. A name listed in
[`CREDENTIAL_ONLY_HEADER_NAMES`] accepts only a `credential` value.

oneOf.description: Sent as written. Not secret: reads return the value.

The token of a static-token credential in this universe, resolved at
each request and sent raw, without a scheme prefix.

ResourceAccessSummary.description:
The audience of a session's or bot's root as views show it: whether it is
shared with the universe, and who created it. A bot's session and a
delegated child show their root's.

createdBy.description: Absent for work whose creator was not recorded.

RunFailureKindView.description: Why a run failed, as the harness classified it.

oneOf.description:
The context no longer fits the model, or holds too many entries to keep
running, and compaction did not bring it down. `message` says what to do.

The provider or the path to it failed the generation, including a generation
the provider cancelled unasked. A run someone cancelled has status `cancelled`
and no failure.

The provider rejected the request as invalid or larger than the model
accepts. `message` is the provider's own text, unchanged; resending the
same context fails the same way.

The provider cut the response off at its output cap. Raising
`maxOutputTokens` or lowering `reasoningEffort` can help; the partial text
stays in context.
The provider refused the request or filtered the response.

The run needed another turn and its `maxTurns` allowed none. Its tool calls
have results and the session stays usable.

The harness refused a step of this run because of what the session holds.
`message` is the refusal's own text. The session stays usable, and open
tool calls were answered as cancelled.

RunFailureView.description:
Why a run failed. `kind` is the harness's classification; `message` is free text
for display, and the provider's own message for `requestRejected`.

maxTurns.description: Model turns this run may start, at least 1, in place of the session's `maxTurns`.

cursor.description: Exclusive upper run-id bound from a previous page.

RunReadResponse.description:
The projection of one run. A run past the server's detail limit keeps its opening
events, so its input renders, and its most recent whole turns, and reports the gap
in `earlierEventsOmitted`; `session/events/read` has the rest. Inline message and
reasoning text is complete. Tool and catalog previews are bounded; their full bodies
remain available through `blobs/read`.

model.description:
Optional model override within the session's provider identity and API
kind. Changing either requires a new session, even before the first run.
Any model on that route is allowed, whatever context the session retains.

notifyOnTerminal.description:
Request a terminal emission to the session's immutable
lifecycle controller. It is delivered to a running controller, which may
hear it more than once; others reconcile through `session/runs/read`.
The destination is derived by the gateway; callers supply only the
controller's opaque dedup token.

submissionId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key, unique per session. Retrying
`session/runs/start` with the same submission id and the same
source/config/terminal notification returns the original run instead
of starting a second one; reusing a submission id with any of those
inputs changed is rejected. The session recognizes it against queued and
active runs and its most recent 256 terminal runs, so a retry older than
that starts a new run.

items.description:
Steering input, same vocabulary as run input. Delivered to the model
at the next turn boundary of the run; it does not interrupt the
in-flight turn or wake a parked run. If the run fails before that
boundary, the input still enters context and the next run sees it as
history. Cancelling the run drops it.

runId.description:
The run to steer. Must be the session's current active run, running or
parked; a queued, finished or cancelling run is rejected so a late steer
never lands on the next run.

submissionId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key. Retrying with the same id and the same items
lands the steering once and returns its original id; reusing the id with other
items is rejected. The run recognizes it among its most recent steering batches.

steeringId.description: Identifier of the accepted steering batch within the session.

RunSummaryView.description:
Bounded run metadata projected from reducer state. Transcript entries and
tool payloads are available only from `session/runs/read` or the event
stream.

failure.description:
Why a failed run failed. The message is cut to a preview here, and
`session/runs/read` has all of it.

usage.description:
Provider usage so far. A summary of a run old enough to be read back from the
session's log has none; `session/runs/read` still totals it.

earlierEventsOmitted.description:
This run is past the server's detail limit: `entries` and `toolBatches` hold
its opening and its most recent turns. `session/events/read` has the turns
between them.

failure.description: Why a failed run failed, with its whole message.

finishedAtMs.description:
When the run reached a terminal state, derived from its committed
completed, failed, or cancelled event. Absent for non-terminal runs.

output.description: Authoritative terminal output, retained independently of active context.

outputText.description:
Complete visible text derived from `output`; absent for non-text output
or runs without a terminal output. Native metadata stays in the blob.

startedAtMs.description:
When the run left the queue and began executing, derived from the
committed `runStarted` event. Absent while the run is queued.

envd.description:
The environment daemon build this release ships. Descriptive: the
gateway admits any daemon that speaks `envd.protocolVersion`,
whatever commit it was built from.

gitSha.description: Full git commit this server was built from.

version.description:
Release version with the git commit as SemVer build metadata, for
example `0.1.0+2093b949…`.

SessionActivity.description:
What a session is doing now. A queued run counts as idle until it starts;
a closed session is idle.

oneOf.description: A run has started and not yet ended.
The active run is parked on approvals: it needs a person.

force.description:
Cancel the active run and drop queued runs instead of rejecting on
active work. Recovers sessions whose workflow no longer exists (e.g.
after an operator terminate) by reconciling the session log directly. A
session that never opened has no log to close, so it is removed and the
call answers `notFound`.

SessionConfig.description:
Session configuration document.

Sparse and capability-oriented: an omitted section means defaults, an
absent feature is not granted (no tools, no access). The document is
replaced whole via `session/config/put`; reads return exactly the stored
document, so read-modify-write round-trips.

model.description:
At creation, omission uses the profile model or universe agentRun
default. On configuration replacement or profile application to an
existing session, omission preserves its current model. Documents read
back from a session always carry the model. Provider identity and API
kind are fixed for the session lifetime. The model name may change at
any time: retained reasoning and compaction state goes to the new model
unchanged, and the provider keeps or drops it. A combination the provider
refuses fails that run as `requestRejected`, and the session stays open.

SessionConfigPutParams.description:
Replace the session config with a complete document. Anything omitted
from the document reverts to defaults; an absent feature is revoked.
Requires an idle session; putting an identical document is a no-op that
leaves the revision untouched.

expectedConfigRevision.description:
Checked against the session's current config revision when present;
absent replaces unconditionally.

cascade.description:
Delete delegated descendants too. False requires the target to be a
closed retention-tree leaf.

sharedOnly.description:
Atomically require every selected session's audience to be shared.
Delegating services use this guard for operators deleting shared work.

softDelete.description:
Hide sessions while retaining records, events, checkpoints and blob roots.
False (the default) permanently deletes them without prior soft deletion.

oneOf.description:
One system-owned workflow-backed tool was durably admitted without
assigning lifecycle ownership to the session.

completionPromises.description:
Keyed completion promises created atomically with the
invocation; absent for accepted invocations.

oneOf.description:
Durable start intent for a start-on-call workflow tool. There is no
successful started event; the deterministic execution id makes the
start replay-safe.

completionPromises.description:
Keyed completion promises created atomically with the start
intent.

executionId.description:
System-derived deterministic execution id of the started plugin
workflow.

requestedBy.description: Who asked, as the API boundary attributed the request.
Who asked, as the API boundary attributed the request.
Who asked, as the API boundary attributed the request.

oneOf.description:
No approval remains and no batch holds the run parked, so it is working
again even if no other event follows for a while.

requestedBy.description:
Who cancelled a run that had not started; a started run records
its requester on the cancellation request.

usage.description:
Provider token usage for this generation, including the
prompt-cache read/write counts, when the provider reported it.

oneOf.description:
The run was cancelled while this turn was open; the turn ended without
a generation result.

Active entries replaced in place by id (`session/context/replace`).
Each keeps its id, position, and kind; the replaced content stays in
the event history.

A compaction was asked for while something else held the context. It waits
for a safe boundary, where `contextCompactionRequested` follows, and the
context revision does not move until then.

One tool call finished. `output_bytes` is the size of the
model-visible text the tool produced before the runtime's projection
budget was applied, absent for synthetic results; `truncated` is true
when that budget cut it.

attachments.description: Files the call linked. Media it supplied arrives as context entries.

oneOf.description:
Progress of a code tool execution. This preserves the contiguous session
event cursor without projecting internal scope bindings or payloads as
conversational tool calls.

before.description: Exclusive upper sequence bound for backward reads only. Must be positive.

direction.description:
Forward reads follow `after`; backward reads select the latest window
below `before` (or the current head when absent). Both return events
chronologically. Backward reads do not replay reducer state.

waitMs.description:
Forward reads only. Long-poll: when no events exist past `after`, hold the request until
one lands or this many milliseconds elapse, then return a normal
(possibly empty) page. Zero or absent preserves immediate return.
Values above the server cap are clamped, not rejected.

complete.description:
No more events in the requested direction at the time of this read.
This does not imply that the session is closed.

events.description:
Events are always chronological, including backward pages. A page may
begin inside a run or tool batch; clients must retain continuation state.

headCursor.description:
Backward reads fence the head before reading. The initial backward
page's head is the starting `after` cursor for live forward reads.
An empty backward read returns sequence zero.

nextCursor.description:
Forward: pass as `after`. Backward: pass as `before` to fetch older
history; absent when the beginning is reached. Never use a backward
continuation to advance a forward live cursor.

SessionExecutionFailureView.description:
How an open session's workflow execution stopped. A session that closed
normally never reports one.

oneOf.description: The execution failed; its error is in the Temporal workflow history.

The execution was ended from outside, or ended without closing the
session.
The execution ran past a Temporal timeout.

Temporal has no execution for this session, for example because a dead
one has passed namespace retention.

SessionJobExitView.description: How a job's root process ended.

oneOf.description: Normal exit with this status code.
Killed by this signal, named like `SIGSEGV`.

offset.description: Byte offset of the chunk's first byte in the job's combined output.

oneOf.description:
Dropped from the middle because the job's retained output exceeded
its cap; the head and the newest bytes are kept.
Released after it was delivered.

SessionJobOutputGapView.description:
Output bytes in `[offset, offset + omittedBytes)` that cannot be
returned.

SessionJobReadEntryView.description:
One job's summary and output page, or why it could not be read: an
entry with `error` and no summary names a job the environment does not
know (never created, or garbage-collected).

outputEnd.description: Output bytes the job produced so far; final once it is terminal.

outputGaps.description:
Output ranges between the requested start and `outputNext` that
cannot be returned.

outputNext.description: Byte offset to continue reading from: pass it as `after`.

SessionJobStatusView.description: Job lifecycle. `queued` and `running` are live; the rest are terminal.

oneOf.description: Waiting for dependencies or its queue.
Exited with code 0.
Exited otherwise, or could not start.
Its timeout expired and it was stopped.
Stopped or never started because of a cancel.
A dependency did not finish as the dependency policy requires.
The environment daemon stopped while the job was queued or running.

SessionJobStoppedByView.description: Why Lightspeed stopped a running job.

oneOf.description: Its timeout expired: terminate, a grace period, then kill.
A cancel without `force`: terminate, a grace period, then kill.
A cancel with `force`: killed at once.

SessionJobSummaryView.description:
What a job is and how it ended. Instants are the environment's wall
clock.

cancelRequestedAtMs.description: When a cancel reached the job while it ran.

durationMs.description: Run time from start to finish, immune to clock jumps.

exit.description: How the job's root process ended, once it ran and exited.

orphanedDescendants.description:
True when the job's root process exited while descendants it spawned
were still running; the host terminated them best-effort at job
completion.

requestId.description: The start request that created the job; part of its identity.

stoppedBy.description: Set when Lightspeed stopped the running job.

SessionListParams.description:
Filters for `session/list`. An unknown field is refused, so a misspelled
filter fails rather than returning a wider list.

closed.description:
Only closed sessions (`true`), or only new and open ones (`false`).
Absent lists both. Every filter here narrows the list, and an absent
one does not filter.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor`.

lifecycleControlled.description:
Only work whose root a lifecycle controller owns (`true`), or work no
controller owns (`false`); sub-agents follow their root. Absent lists
both.

metadata.description:
Only sessions matching every entry (AND semantics). A non-empty value
requires an exact key/value pair; an empty value requires key presence.

parent.description: Only sub-agent sessions this session delegated directly.

subagent.description:
Only sub-agent sessions (`true`), or only root sessions (`false`).
Absent lists both.

trees.description: Only these root sessions and all their sub-agents.

visibleTo.description:
Only sessions whose root is shared with the universe or was created
by this actor: what that actor sees as a non-administrator.

nextCursor.description:
Present when more sessions exist past this page. Ordering is most
recently updated first; pages can drift under concurrent activity.

SessionMetadataPutParams.description:
Replace a session's metadata with a complete map (the same bounds as
`session/start`). Record-only: it does not touch the event log or
`updatedAtMs`. There is no merge form; read, edit, and put.

metadata.description: The complete new map; empty clears it.

SessionMutationView.description:
Compact acknowledgement returned by session mutations. Call
`session/read` when the complete current-state summary is needed.

SessionOriginView.description:
Typed provenance of a delegated (sub-agent) session: who created it,
under which root, at what depth, and the effective limits it was spawned
with. Provenance, never ownership — the child is an ordinary session.

depth.description: Absolute depth from the root; a root's direct child is 1.

invocationId.description: The workflow-tool invocation that created the child.

rootSessionId.description:
Nearest ancestor without an origin; root-scoped limits count every
session naming this root.

runLimit.description:
Newest run summaries to include. Values above the server maximum are
clamped.

displayName.description: New display name; absent clears it. Cannot contain NUL.

restarted.description: A new execution started. False when one was already running.

deleteAfterCloseMs.description: Positive duration enables automatic tree soft deletion; null disables it.

SessionRetentionView.description:
Effective tree-owned retention for a session. Delegated children name their
owning root and project that root's policy and deadline.

access.description:
Audience of the new session, set atomically with its creation. Absent
means unshared until `session/share`; a retry keeps the original.

deleteAfterCloseMs.description:
Root-owned automatic soft deletion measured from close. Absent inherits a
profile default, explicit null keeps the tree, and a duration overrides
the profile.

integration.description:
Immutable lifecycle controller and workflow tools connecting this session
to outside workflows, admitted only when it is first created, with bound
dispatch stated explicitly. This document is not part of `SessionConfig`
and cannot be changed through `session/config/put`. Retrying an id with an
integration requires the same one, and a session started without one
cannot gain one. Any retry of an integrated session answers
`sessionExecutionStopped` for a stopped workflow execution instead of
restarting it.

metadata.description:
Descriptive key/value metadata, applied only when the session is
first created: at most 32 entries, keys 1..=64 bytes, values 1..=256
bytes, no control characters, no `lightspeed.` prefix. It never
affects routing, authority, or selection; filter on it with
`session/list`.

access.description:
The audience of the session's root: whether it is shared with the
universe, and who created it.

activity.description:
What the session is doing now: idle, working on a run, or waiting for
an approval.

lifecycleControlled.description: True only when the session's integration names a lifecycle controller.

metadata.description: Descriptive key/value metadata; empty when none was set.

origin.description: Sub-agent lineage; absent for root sessions.

access.description:
The audience of the session's root: whether it is shared with the
universe, and who created it.

activeEnvironmentId.description: The universe environment selected by the session event log.

activeRun.description:
The currently executing run, always present when one exists — the
paged `runs` window can omit it behind newer queued runs, so control
surfaces (steering, status) must read it from here.

activity.description:
What the session is doing now: idle, working on a run, or waiting for
an approval. Lists carry the same value.

config.description:
The stored sparse config document, exactly as last put (model and
feature versions materialized at admission). Effective tool reality
is visible via `active_tools`.

executionFailure.description:
Set by `session/read` when the session is still open but its workflow
execution has stopped. Nothing is running and the rest of the view is
the stored log, so `activity` can still say what it last did. Lists do not check
the execution, so a list and a read of the same session can differ.

integration.description:
Immutable workflow integration. A lifecycle controller indicates external
session ownership; a tools-only integration does not.

lifecycleControlled.description: True only when the session's integration names a lifecycle controller.

lifecycleStatus.description:
Whether the session has opened or closed. What it is doing while open is
`activity`, and whether its workflow is still there is `executionFailure`.

metadata.description: Descriptive key/value metadata; empty when none was set.

origin.description: Sub-agent lineage; absent for root sessions.

SkillCatalogView.description: An independent catalog instance; sources are never merged or used as fallbacks.

location.description: Where to read the instructions and resolve supporting files.

SkillLocationView.description: Readable paths within the owning catalog's filesystem domain.

SubagentAgentPin.description: The profile a sub-agent was spawned from, pinned at its revision.

runTimeoutMs.description: Absent when a child's run has no time limit.

SubagentsFeature.description:
Grants sub-agent delegation: `agent_run` (joined, result inline) and
`agent_spawn` (promise, joined with `await`) over the listed agent
profiles. Limits are root-scoped and attenuating: every descendant of a
root session counts against the root, and a nested grant can narrow but
never widen the limits pinned on its origin.

agents.description:
The agent menu. Every id must name an existing profile; the model
picks by id and reads descriptions from the sub-agent catalog.

maxConcurrent.description: Open sessions under the root at any time, excluding the root.

maxDepth.description: A child at depth `d` may spawn only while `d + 1 <= maxDepth`.

runTimeoutMs.description: Per-child run deadline in milliseconds. Omit it for no time limit.

TimersFeature.description:
Grants timer promises through the sleep tool plus the base concurrency
tools (await/cancel/detach).

ToolAttachmentView.description:
A file a completed tool call supplied, linked by name rather than shown to the
model. Media a call supplied is in `media` on the call and in context entries.

blobRef.description: Full immutable blob identity; read through the universe-scoped blob API.

handle.description: Model-facing alias, resolved against recorded attachments.

ToolCallDisplayGroup.description:
Coarse activity family of a tool call, chosen by the projection from the
tool name. Clients key icons and colours on it; the verb and target carry
the specifics. Unknown tools land in `Other`.

oneOf.description: Reads the environment or the web without changing it.
Writes or patches files.
Runs or controls a process.
Orchestrates tool calls in a code-mode script.

Calls a tool on an MCP server, through the builtin bridge or a
provider-hosted MCP block.
Delegates to a sub-agent or waits on one.
Bot-to-bot traffic and a bot's own configuration tools.
Sends into a chat conversation on a channel.

toolId.description: Admitted registry identity, absent when the model used an unavailable name.

ToolCallMediaView.description: One media item a tool call handed the model.

handle.description:
`media:` plus the first twelve hex characters of `blobRef`; what the
model calls this item.

arguments.description: Bounded preview; `argumentsRef` has the full body.

attachments.description:
Files the call linked, which the model does not get as input. Media it supplied
is in `media`.

durationMs.description:
Execution milliseconds measured by the runtime around the call body;
the remainder of the started/completed window is overhead.

finishedAtMs.description:
When the call's terminal result was committed. The window to
`startedAtMs` includes runtime scheduling overhead.

media.description:
Media the call handed the model (MCP images and documents, file
reads, sub-agent hand-offs), in the order the model saw it. Each item
is also a user-role media entry of the run; fetch bytes with
`blobs/read`.

output.description: Bounded preview of the model-visible result; `outputRef` has the full body.

outputBytes.description:
Bytes of model-visible text the tool produced before the runtime applied its
budget, from the call's `toolCallCompleted` event.

startedAtMs.description:
When the call was dispatched for execution, from the committed
`toolCallStarted` event. Absent until dispatch.

toolId.description: Admitted registry identity, absent when the model used an unavailable name.

truncated.description:
The runtime cut the model-visible text to its budget, from the call's
`toolCallCompleted` event. This is separate from the preview bound above.

oneOf.description: Code-owned definition; names and schemas are resolved for each turn.

TranscriptionAudio.description: Immutable audio input in this universe's content store.

idempotencyKey.description:
Scoped to the requester. Matching retries rejoin the original job,
including after defaults change; changed requests conflict. Identity is
retained for the Temporal namespace's workflow-history retention period.

transcriptRef.description:
Plain UTF-8 transcript blob, usable as ordinary textRef input.
Unsubmitted content can be swept after the ordinary CAS grace period.

oneOf.description: The provider rejected the request instead of serving it.

UniverseAction.description:
What a public method does, independent of its RPC spelling. Requests are
gated by their key's groups; this classifies what the runtime's own work
may do and which role a gate built on the contract should require.

oneOf.description: Share an unshared session with the universe.
Use a workspace, environment or MCP server, or store bytes.

Configure a workspace, environment, MCP server or shared
configuration such as credentials and channels.

VfsFeature.description:
Grants the session virtual filesystem. Workspace attachments declare the
session-visible namespace and the VFS catalog is surfaced. The file tool
surface is derived from the attachments: any attachment installs the read
tools, any `edit` attachment adds the write tools, and with the
environments feature granted the matching transfer tools appear. `{}`
grants a VFS with no attachments, no tools, and no sourcing.

prompts.description:
Prompt-instruction sourcing from the VFS. Absent disables loading;
an empty block discovers conventional attached roots.

skills.description:
Independent VFS skill discovery. Absent disables discovery and removes
its runtime catalog; an empty block discovers conventional attached roots.

workingDirectory.description: Absolute VFS tool working directory; absent uses /.

workspaces.description:
Catalog resources exposed in the session's workspace namespace at
disjoint absolute paths.

roots.description:
Absent searches .agents/prompts and .lightspeed/prompts beneath each
workspace attachment. Explicit roots replace these defaults and must be
non-empty absolute paths contained in workspace attachments.

Absent searches .agents/skills and .lightspeed/skills beneath each
workspace attachment. Explicit roots replace these defaults and must be
non-empty absolute paths contained in workspace attachments.

snapshotRef.description:
Snapshot to seed the workspace from. Absent starts the workspace from
the empty snapshot, committed server-side.

VfsWorkspaceFileReadParams.description: Read a file from a workspace's current head, by path.

bytes.description: Total byte size of the head snapshot.

files.description: File count of the head snapshot.

Visibility.description:
Who sees a root's tree. Sessions start unshared (`restricted`) and are
shared with the universe once, one way; everything else is shared.

WebFeature.description:
Grants network access through the web toolset; `fetch` and `search` are
independently granted, and a web block granting neither is rejected.

allowedDomains.description: Absent means all domains; an explicit list must be non-empty.

WebhookVerification.description:
How an inbound webhook proves it comes from the sender: possession of
the URL token, or additionally an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with a
secret leased from a retrievable grant.

WorkflowStartRefInput.description:
Opaque reference to a workflow-substrate recipe already stored through
the blob API. The fingerprint authenticates the exact recipe bytes used
by the workflow-start adapter.

WorkflowToolCompletionInput.description:
Completion contract for one workflow-tool invocation. Joined tools park
the original call on one runtime-owned reply; Promises exposes handles for
model-controlled concurrency.

deadlineAfterMs.description:
Hard deadline for the reply, in milliseconds. Required for a bound
receiver, which has no other way to free a caller it never answers.
A started execution may omit it, because the recovery poll detects
an execution that died.

WorkflowToolCompletionKeySourceInput.description: Declarative promise-key derivation over schema-validated tool arguments.

oneOf.description: The single reserved `reply` key.
A JSON Pointer to an array of unique completion-key strings.

A JSON Pointer to an array of objects; the named string field of
every item is its completion key, so the model's own name for a work
item keys that item's promise.

A JSON Pointer to an array; keys are `prefix` joined with each item's
zero-based index.

workflowToolId.description:
The workflow-tool namespace: what invocations and bindings are keyed on. The
registry identity the model sees through `activeTools` is `tool.name`.

name.description: Function name exposed to the model and used as its registry identity.

WorkflowToolTargetInput.description:
Lifecycle target of a workflow-backed tool. Bound tools deliver to an
existing execution; start tools create an execution from an immutable,
CAS-backed recipe for every invocation.

WorkspaceAttachment.description:
One catalog resource mounted into the session namespace. Exactly one of
`workspaceId` and `snapshotRef` names the resource; snapshots are
immutable and must be attached with `read` access.

info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST /rpc. Results are wrapped in the AgentApiOutcome envelope; session events are consumed via session/events/read cursor pagination. An authenticated gateway answers a request without a valid API key with HTTP 401 and a JSON-RPC error whose id is null, before it reads the request body. An error decided for a request that was read is a JSON-RPC error for that request's id.
info.title: Lightspeed Agent API

methods.description: Reads bytes at a path in the current workspace head.
methods.name: vfs/workspaces/files/read

methods.description: Returns protocol version, server identity, credential scope and allowed groups before universe selection. Requires authentication in authenticated mode; no universe header is accepted.
methods.name: initialize

methods.description: Creates a session, unshared unless access says universe, with optional config, profile and immutable integration. Explicit values override profile metadata and retention; the default environment attachment becomes active. Retrying an id returns it and restarts a stopped execution from its log, unless integrated. Failed setup closes a server-allocated id.
methods.name: session/start

methods.description: Returns stored state plus a bounded newest-first run-summary page, and needs no worker. An open session whose execution has stopped reports executionFailure. Follow nextRunCursor with session/runs/list when hasOlderRuns is true; use session/events/read for the transcript.
methods.name: session/read

methods.description: Returns a cursor-paginated summary list ordered by most recent update, optionally narrowed by filters such as visibleTo, which keeps sessions whose root is shared with the universe or was created by that actor. An unknown parameter is refused. Pages may shift while sessions are changing.
methods.name: session/list

methods.description: Replaces the complete sparse config while the session is idle. Use the current config revision for safe read-modify-write; omitted features are revoked, an omitted model preserves the current model, and an identical document is a no-op. A newly attached MCP server must be usable; a held one that has gone away only drops out of later runs.
methods.name: session/config/put

methods.description: Sets the display name, or clears it when displayName is omitted.
methods.name: session/rename

methods.description: Replaces the complete descriptive key/value map (bounded like session/start); an omitted or empty map clears it. Record-only: the event log and updatedAtMs are untouched.
methods.name: session/metadata/put

methods.description: Sets the positive close-relative automatic soft-deletion duration on a retention root, or clears it with null. Delegated children inherit the root policy and cannot override it. Retention does not permanently delete stored history.
methods.name: session/retention/put

methods.description: Starts a new workflow execution for an open session whose last one stopped, from its log. A run that was not parked fails, a parked run keeps waiting, and queued runs start afterwards. A running session is left alone. Refused for a closed session and for one with no run history.
methods.name: session/restart

methods.description: Closes an idle session and detaches its environment bindings. Without force, active work of any kind, including a pending detached promise, rejects the call. Force mode cancels active work, drops queued runs, and can recover a session whose workflow is unavailable.
methods.name: session/close

methods.description: Permanently deletes a closed retention-tree leaf, or its closed delegated-child subtree when cascade is true. Set softDelete to true to hide sessions while retaining records and history until a deployment administrator purges them. Prior soft deletion is not required for permanent deletion.
methods.name: session/delete

methods.description: Moves an unshared root session to universe visibility, one way; its delegated children follow it. Refused on a bot's session, a delegated child, and a session already shared. Core applies it for any caller of the method; who may share is the caller's gate's decision.
methods.name: session/share
methods.summary: Share a session with the universe

methods.description: Returns chronological events. Forward (default) follows after and supports long-polling. Backward reads the latest window below before (or the head); pass nextCursor as before until complete. Follow live events after the initial backward headCursor. Windows may split runs/tool batches; keep historical reconstruction separate from live controls.
methods.name: session/events/read

methods.description: Admits a batch of keyed context entries with per-entry results. The same content under a key is a no-op. Different content replaces the earlier entry, which leaves active context, and goes last under a new id; a catalog supersedes instead. Invalid input can fail one entry without discarding successful entries.
methods.name: session/context/append

methods.description: Removes active entries by stable key with per-key results. Missing keys are idempotent no-ops; runtime-reserved run keys cannot be removed.
methods.name: session/context/remove

methods.description: Replaces active tool results and user messages in place by entry id, with per-entry results, e.g. to withdraw content the provider rejects. Entries keep their ids, positions, and kinds, so a tool result takes only text and its call stays answered. Refused while a run is active; ids no longer in context report absent.
methods.name: session/context/replace

methods.description: Performs one standalone compaction in any automatic mode, including Disabled, and waits for its outcome. Active work queues it until a safe turn boundary. A failed compaction leaves the context unchanged and fails the call with its reason. A wait that runs out fails with operationPending while it can still complete; session events report the outcome.
methods.name: session/context/compact

methods.description: Returns once the run is accepted — queued behind an active run, or running — not when it finishes. A compacting session holds the request; if the wait runs out the call fails with operationPending and the submission id, and the run still starts later. Retrying with that id cannot start a second run. Follow session events or reread the session.
methods.name: session/runs/start

methods.description: Returns a newest-first keyset page of bounded run summaries, from current state for recent runs and from the session's log for older ones.
methods.name: session/runs/list

methods.description: Projects one run from its events. A run past the server's detail limit keeps its opening and its most recent turns and sets earlierEventsOmitted; session/events/read has the rest.
methods.name: session/runs/read

methods.description: Requests cancellation of the named queued or active run and returns its summary; observe session events for terminal completion. In-flight model and tool activity is aborted; no grace turn runs.
methods.name: session/runs/cancel

methods.description: Approves or rejects pending MCP tool calls on the named active run. Valid decisions apply independently; the run resumes only after every pending approval has a decision. A decision whose wait runs out reports status pending and can still apply.
methods.name: session/runs/approvals/decide

methods.description: Injects input into the named active run; the model sees it at the next turn boundary without interrupting the in-flight turn. A parked run holds it without waking. Rejected for queued, cancelling, or finished runs. Supply submissionId so a retry lands once; a wait that runs out fails with operationPending and the steering can still land.
methods.name: session/runs/steer

methods.description: Returns separate VFS and environment catalogs with source, reference, availability, readable skill paths, and warnings. Refreshes only when open with no active or queued run, without waking environments. Absent catalogs are omitted.
methods.name: session/skills/list

methods.description: Applies a named or inline profile's config, instructions, and environment setup to an existing session; mutating profile sections require it to be open and idle. Pass current revisions to guard concurrent changes.
methods.name: session/profiles/apply
methods.summary: Apply a profile to a session

methods.description: Selects an attached, live universe environment for environment-targeted tools while the session is idle.
methods.name: session/environments/activate

methods.description: Clears active environment selection without changing or closing the universe environment.
methods.name: session/environments/deactivate

methods.description: Maps an environment variable name to a retrievable credential grant or to a model API key provider's stored key. Commands in the environment receive the plain value, so a brokered grant and any other provider credential are refused. Requires configuring resources in the universe. The response exposes only the source handle, never secret material.
methods.name: environments/credentials/bind
methods.summary: Bind a credential into an environment

methods.description: Returns variable names and credential source handles for a universe environment; resolved secret values are never returned.
methods.name: environments/credentials/list

methods.description: Removes one variable-to-credential mapping without deleting the underlying grant or provider credential.
methods.name: environments/credentials/unbind

methods.description: Creates a provisioned environment, attributed to the caller, from a template of a provider enabled for the universe. Idempotent per requestId: same inputs, same environment; others conflict. Provisioning until the target's first envd handshake, then open; idle overrides the template default.
methods.name: environments/create

methods.description: Returns one environment: its source, lifecycle state, derived display status, state message, close reason, daemon build, and the latest provider observation.
methods.name: environments/read

methods.description: Replaces the display name and caller metadata of an environment of any kind. Refused for a closed environment.
methods.name: environments/update

methods.description: Lists the universe environments in id order, one page at a time, optionally filtered by provider, registration key, state, or metadata. Closed environments are omitted unless includeClosed is set or state is closed. Continue from nextAfter.
methods.name: environments/list

methods.description: Closes an environment; idempotent. A provisioned environment moves to closing while Lightspeed asks its provider to remove the target, retrying until it is gone, then closed. External and registered environments close at once, and a connected registered daemon is told its environment closed.
methods.name: environments/close

methods.description: Creates an open environment backed by a Lightspeed-reachable envd endpoint, attributed to the caller. Idempotent per requestId. Reachability is checked on use.
methods.name: environments/external/create

methods.description: Declares a fixed machine as an open environment with a chosen id before its daemon registers. The first daemon its persistent key admits under the given name is bound to it; until then it is away and tools wait. Repeating it changes nothing; display name and metadata converge. The key and name are fixed. Conflict: an id or name in use.
methods.name: environments/registered/put

methods.description: Forgets the daemon bound to a declared environment and ends its connection, so another daemon identity may bind under the same key and name. The environment keeps its id, its name, its credential bindings and every reference to it. No effect when no daemon is bound. Refused for an environment that was not declared.
methods.name: environments/registered/release

methods.description: Synchronously ensures or removes public ingress of an open provisioned environment through its provider; source.publicEndpoint carries the reported endpoint. Rejected when the provider offers no ingress; an internal error, safe to retry, when the provider is unreachable or times out. The provider owns hostname, guest port, routing, TLS, and health.
methods.name: environments/ingress/put

methods.description: Synchronously moves an open provisioned environment's target to running, paused, suspended, or stopped via its provider and records the observation; the provider may also change power on idle. Rejected without provider power control or when the template lacks the state; an internal error, safe to retry, when the provider is unreachable or times out.
methods.name: environments/power/put

methods.description: Lists this universe's bindings to deployment providers and whether each is enabled.
methods.name: environments/provider-bindings/list

methods.description: Returns this universe's binding to one provider. Templates and physical resource, network, and ingress policy remain provider-owned.
methods.name: environments/provider-bindings/read

methods.description: Reads templates live from the controllers of the universe's enabled provider bindings, or of one provider: compute, power states, public ingress, and default idle policy.
methods.name: environments/templates/list

methods.description: Returns one template, read live from a bound provider's controller.
methods.name: environments/templates/read

methods.description: Starts a dependency-aware job group on one environment instance, injecting its configured credentials at provider start. requestId is the retry identity; jobs are owned by the instance, not a session. A powered-down environment wakes on its data route; the call fails with environmentNotReady while it wakes or reconnects; retry with backoff.
methods.name: environments/jobs/create

methods.description: Reads selected job handles with bounded output from a byte offset or the output tail; continue from each entry's outputNext and poll on the returned status.
methods.name: environments/jobs/read

methods.description: Requests cancellation for selected jobs, optionally including dependents. Force is provider-specific escalation; inspect each per-job result.
methods.name: environments/jobs/cancel

methods.description: Creates a reusable universe-scoped key that lets outbound envd daemons register as environments. The plaintext secret is returned exactly once; only its hash is stored. Identity mode (immutable), active limit, disconnect grace, offline close-after, and expiry are the key's policy. Treat the secret like a cluster-join credential.
methods.name: environments/registration-keys/create

methods.description: Makes the key of this id exist with this policy and answer to exactly the supplied secret. Repeating it changes nothing. A missing key is created; a different secret retires the previous one at once, as rotation does. Conflict: a changed identity mode, a revoked key, or a secret that is or was a key's.
methods.name: environments/registration-keys/put

methods.description: Returns the key's display prefix, policy, status, and derived environment counts; never the secret or its hash.
methods.name: environments/registration-keys/read

methods.description: Lists this universe's registration keys with policy, status, and derived counts. Each key is the group of the environments it admitted.
methods.name: environments/registration-keys/list

methods.description: Replaces a key's editable policy: display name, active limit, disconnect grace, offline close-after, and expiry; an omitted field is unset. The identity mode is immutable. The active limit and expiry apply to later admissions; a changed disconnect grace or offline close-after applies at the next sweep to environments whose daemon is away.
methods.name: environments/registration-keys/update

methods.description: Replaces the key's secret and display prefix and retires the old secret at once. The key keeps its id, group, policy, and the environments it admitted; daemons already registered are unaffected because they never present the key again. Returns the new secret once. Refused for a revoked key.
methods.name: environments/registration-keys/rotate

methods.description: Stops the key from admitting new daemon identities; already registered daemons keep reconnecting. With closeEnvironments, also closes every non-closed environment the key admitted. Idempotent.
methods.name: environments/registration-keys/revoke

methods.description: Admit or rejoin a requester-scoped audio transcription. The resolved model is immutable. No session or run is created.
methods.name: transcriptions/start

methods.description: Read status and transcript text. An asserted actor may only read their own drafts; direct universe keys retain method-group authority. Unsubmitted CAS results may expire.
methods.name: transcriptions/read

methods.description: Cancel unfinished transcription. Repeated cancellation is safe; completed results remain unchanged. An asserted actor may only cancel their own drafts; direct universe keys retain method-group authority.
methods.name: transcriptions/cancel

methods.description: Returns the revision and independent agentRun and speechToText selections. Revision zero means no update has been made. Does not contact model providers.
methods.name: models/defaults/read

methods.description: Sets or explicitly clears one purpose slot. With expectedRevision the write is refused if the defaults changed since. Existing sessions and admitted work keep their model. Validates the purpose and protocol without contacting provider discovery.
methods.name: models/defaults/put

methods.description: Queries supported providers directly, with a brief process-local burst cache, and returns best-effort selectable routes. One provider failure does not discard successful results from others.
methods.name: models/list

methods.description: Creates a new universe-scoped reusable profile document; use profiles/put for create-or-replace revision semantics.
methods.name: profiles/create

methods.description: Returns the complete profile document and current revision.
methods.name: profiles/read

methods.description: Returns lightweight summaries of universe-scoped reusable profiles.
methods.name: profiles/list

methods.description: Stores the complete profile document. Use expectedRevision from profiles/read when replacing to prevent lost updates; absence writes unconditionally.
methods.name: profiles/put
methods.summary: Create or replace an agent profile

methods.description: Deletes the catalog document; sessions previously created or configured from it retain their materialized state.
methods.name: profiles/delete

methods.description: Decodes and stores a batch of base64 payloads, returning immutable content references in request order. Re-uploading identical bytes is naturally deduplicated.
methods.name: blobs/put

methods.description: Returns the complete immutable blob of this universe as base64; large values count against gateway and MCP response limits.
methods.name: blobs/read

methods.description: Checks a batch of content references without returning blob bodies, preserving request order.
methods.name: blobs/has

methods.description: Validates and stores an immutable filesystem manifest. Upload referenced file blobs first; the returned snapshot ref is content-addressed.
methods.name: vfs/snapshots/commit

methods.description: Returns an immutable snapshot manifest and aggregate file/byte counts; file bodies remain separate blobs.
methods.name: vfs/snapshots/read

methods.description: Creates a universe workspace attributed to the caller at an optional seed snapshot; absence starts from a server-created empty snapshot.
methods.name: vfs/workspaces/create

methods.description: Returns workspace metadata, current head snapshot, and revision for safe updates.
methods.name: vfs/workspaces/read

methods.description: Lists the mutable universe workspaces with head snapshots, sizes, and revisions.
methods.name: vfs/workspaces/list

methods.description: Moves the workspace head to an existing snapshot, which requires use of the workspace, and updates its display name, which requires configuring it. Pass expectedRevision from a read to prevent lost updates.
methods.name: vfs/workspaces/update

methods.description: Deletes the mutable workspace record; immutable snapshots and blobs remain content-addressed resources.
methods.name: vfs/workspaces/delete

methods.description: Stores the complete catalog document with its optional auth-grant credential. A new server is attributed to the caller. Use expectedRevision when replacing; token material is never accepted or returned, but serverUrl is stored and shown as written, so keep secrets out of it.
methods.name: mcp/servers/put
methods.summary: Create or replace an MCP server record

methods.description: Looks for standards-based OAuth protected-resource metadata without creating a server, OAuth client, flow, or grant. An absent OAuth result is inconclusive and callers must allow manual auth selection.
methods.name: mcp/servers/auth/discover

methods.description: Connects directly to the configured MCP server with its current universe credential and returns one bounded live tools/list result. The inventory is never persisted or cached and no tool is invoked.
methods.name: mcp/servers/tools/discover

methods.description: Returns one catalog document with defaults, auth policy, non-secret grant binding, status, and revision; no credential value is exposed.
methods.name: mcp/servers/read

methods.description: Lists the universe catalog entries, optionally filtered by lifecycle/configuration status.
methods.name: mcp/servers/list

methods.description: Deletes the catalog document. Existing session configs that reference it are not silently rewritten and may need explicit reconfiguration.
methods.name: mcp/servers/delete

methods.description: Accepts a plaintext token, encrypts it immediately, and returns only grant metadata/token-presence flags. Brokered is the default; exposure is immutable, and only a retrievable credential can be leased to a service or bound into an environment.
methods.name: auth/grants/import

methods.description: Service callers only. Resolves the current access token through the broker, records the lease, and returns it once. Cache only in memory until expiry minus margin (or at most five minutes without expiry), re-lease after target 401/403, and never persist or place the token in workflow payloads.
methods.name: auth/grants/lease

methods.description: Returns creator attribution, provider binding, scopes, audience, expiry, status, and token-presence flags; access and refresh token values are never returned.
methods.name: auth/grants/read

methods.description: Lists non-secret grant metadata for the universe, optionally filtered by status.
methods.name: auth/grants/list

methods.description: Makes the token credential of this id exist with these settings and hold exactly the supplied token, encrypted on receipt. Repeating it changes nothing. A missing credential is created; a different token replaces the stored one for everything referencing the id. Conflict: another kind of grant, a revoked one, or changed exposure.
methods.name: auth/grants/put

methods.description: Marks the grant unusable by token consumers while retaining non-secret audit metadata.
methods.name: auth/grants/revoke

methods.description: Stores provider endpoints and client identity; an optional plaintext client secret is encrypted and represented thereafter only by hasClientSecret.
methods.name: auth/clients/create

methods.description: Returns endpoints, public client identity, defaults, and secret-presence state; the client secret is never returned.
methods.name: auth/clients/read

methods.description: Lists non-secret OAuth client registrations in the universe.
methods.name: auth/clients/list

methods.description: Deletes the client registration and its stored client secret; grants already created from it remain separate records.
methods.name: auth/clients/delete

methods.description: Creates a short-lived PKCE flow carrying the immutable grant exposure choice and returns a browser authorization URL containing one-time state. Treat the URL as sensitive and poll auth/flows/read for completion.
methods.name: auth/flows/start

methods.description: Polls a flow's pending/completed/failed/expired state and returns the resulting grant id when authorization succeeds; no token value is exposed.
methods.name: auth/flows/read

methods.description: Creates a model or GitHub credential source. Plaintext API keys/private keys are encrypted on receipt and later represented only by configuration plus hasCredential.
methods.name: auth/providers/create

methods.description: Makes the provider of this id exist with this configuration and credential. Repeating it changes nothing. A missing provider is created; one that differs is rewritten in place after the new settings validate, atomically, and its old credential deleted. Sessions and environment variables referencing the id keep working.
methods.name: auth/providers/put

methods.description: Returns provider kind, non-secret configuration, credential-presence state, and status; stored credentials are never returned.
methods.name: auth/providers/read

methods.description: Lists non-secret model/GitHub provider registrations for the universe.
methods.name: auth/providers/list

methods.description: Deletes the provider registration and its directly stored credential; separately stored grants remain independent records.
methods.name: auth/providers/delete

methods.description: Uses the registered GitHub App provider credential to query accessible installations and returns account/permission metadata without tokens.
methods.name: auth/github/installations/list

methods.description: Creates or refreshes a universe auth grant for one accessible installation. This method never returns a token: the broker mints short-lived installation tokens when the grant is used. Brokered is the default; only a grant created retrievable can be bound into an environment or leased to a service.
methods.name: auth/github/installations/grant
methods.summary: Grant access to a GitHub App installation

methods.description: Creates the bot record, optionally with its triggers, and starts its controller. Fails if the bot id exists; a trigger failure rolls the bot back. Returns the created triggers' ingest paths and pairing codes by trigger id.
methods.name: bots/create

methods.description: Replaces the mutable configuration whole and signals the controller, which applies it at its next idle boundary. Pass expectedRevision when replacing; a closed bot accepts label-only edits.
methods.name: bots/put
methods.summary: Create or replace a bot document

methods.description: Returns the bot record, its current revision, and lifecycle columns.
methods.name: bots/read

methods.description: Returns the roster: every bot with its trigger count, pending event count, and latest event, optionally narrowed by createdBy.
methods.name: bots/list

methods.description: Terminal and idempotent: disables every trigger, drops schedules, and tells the controller to archive pending events and force-close its sessions. Returns once signalled; follow bots/state/read for closing to closed.
methods.name: bots/close

methods.description: Closes the bot if needed, waits for its controller to complete, retains its session history, and removes the record so the bot id is free again.
methods.name: bots/delete

methods.description: Queries the controller workflow for its live snapshot (sessions, buffers, active and recent deliveries, budget) and lists sub-agent descendants. The controller is absent until the bot's first event.
methods.name: bots/state/read

methods.description: Asks the controller to close one of the bot's sessions at its next idle boundary and continue on a fresh generation; queued deliveries follow.
methods.name: bots/sessions/rotate

methods.description: Validates the trigger document (CEL parses, grants exist, one inbox per bot, chat routes per conversation), reconciles its Temporal Schedule, and stores it. A poll spec edit resets the cursor; a webhook keeps its URL token. Returns the trigger's ingest path or pairing code beside the view.
methods.name: bots/triggers/put

methods.description: Returns one trigger with its incidents and cursor. The ingest path and pairing code are never part of it; bots/triggers/secrets/read returns them.
methods.name: bots/triggers/read

methods.description: Returns every trigger of the bot ordered by id, without ingest paths or pairing codes.
methods.name: bots/triggers/list

methods.description: Returns a webhook trigger's ingest path, whose token lets the holder post events to the bot, or a chat trigger's pairing code, which connects a conversation to it. Both are absent for other triggers. Needs bot management, unlike reading the trigger.
methods.name: bots/triggers/secrets/read

methods.description: Drops the trigger's Temporal Schedule and pairings, then the record; stored events keep their history.
methods.name: bots/triggers/delete

methods.description: Stores an operator-authored event for the bot's main session and wakes the controller. eventId is the dedupe identity; a duplicate returns the stored row.
methods.name: bots/events/admit

methods.description: Re-admits the stored envelope as a fresh event with the original routing; the replay never coalesces.
methods.name: bots/events/replay

methods.description: Cursor-paginated event log, newest first, with outcomes; payload documents stay in the CAS.
methods.name: bots/events/list

methods.description: Returns the event row and its full stored envelope document.
methods.name: bots/events/read

methods.description: Evaluates a filter against one payload or a sample of recent stored events, reporting matches and evaluation errors without changing anything.
methods.name: bots/filters/test

methods.description: Registers a provider account (Telegram, WhatsApp) for this universe. The credential is a retrievable grant reference; no token is accepted here.
methods.name: channels/accounts/create

methods.description: Replaces the account document whole; pass expectedRevision when replacing. The connector host picks the change up on its next discovery pass.
methods.name: channels/accounts/put
methods.summary: Create or replace a channel account

methods.description: Returns the account document and revision.
methods.name: channels/accounts/read

methods.description: Lists this universe's provider accounts, optionally by provider.
methods.name: channels/accounts/list

methods.description: Removes the account and its pairings; chat triggers that reference it stop serving conversations.
methods.name: channels/accounts/delete

methods.description: Service callers only. Resolves the chat trigger for the conversation, applies pairing, and signals the conversation workflow. Returns the decision so the connector can send pairing prompts itself; acknowledge the provider only after this returns.
methods.name: channels/inbound/admit

methods.description: Lists conversations paired to chat triggers, optionally by account or bot.
methods.name: channels/pairings/list

methods.description: Removes one pairing; the conversation must present the pairing code again to reconnect.
methods.name: channels/pairings/delete

methods.description: Queries the conversation workflow's live state for one chat, for debugging; absent when no workflow exists yet.
methods.name: channels/conversations/read

methods.description: Administrative metadata for soft-deleted sessions, ordered by session ID. Unavailable through universe-scoped methods.
methods.name: deployment/sessions/deleted/list

methods.description: Removes a soft-deleted session and its soft-deleted history subtree. Rejects any selected session that has not been soft-deleted. Releases event, checkpoint and blob references; unreferenced blobs follow normal garbage collection. Does not delete external workspaces, environments, backups or Temporal history.
methods.name: deployment/sessions/purge

methods.description: Deployment configuration inventory of one universe's provider bindings.
methods.name: deployment/environment-provider-bindings/list
methods.summary: List a universe's deployment provider bindings

methods.description: Creates the deployment tenant boundary for an explicit UUID, under the given handle or one derived from the UUID. The operation is idempotent and reports whether a new universe was created; an existing universe keeps its handle. A handle another universe holds is a conflict.
methods.name: deployment/universes/create

methods.description: Returns deployment-wide universe summaries with approximate live aggregate counts and last session activity.
methods.name: deployment/universes/list

methods.description: Returns one deployment tenant summary, addressed by UUID or handle, with aggregate session, workspace, profile, and blob usage.
methods.name: deployment/universes/read

methods.description: Changes the deployment-unique handle without changing the universe UUID or resources. The previous handle is released: requests and URLs that use it stop reaching this universe, and another universe may claim it. Claiming another universe's handle returns a conflict. Does not create a universe.
methods.name: deployment/universes/handle/put

methods.description: Permanently terminates live session workflows, deletes external blob objects, and cascades universe data. The purge is resumable/idempotent after partial failure.
methods.name: deployment/universes/delete

methods.description: Mints a key for a universe or the deployment with the method groups it may call and whether it may assert actors, under the given key id or an allocated one. The plaintext secret is returned exactly once and cannot be recovered. A key id already used in the scope is a conflict.
methods.name: deployment/api-keys/create

methods.description: Makes the key of this id and scope exist, answer to exactly the supplied secret, and hold these groups and name. Repeating it changes nothing. A missing key is created; a different secret replaces the previous one at once. Conflict: a changed actor flag, a revoked key, or a secret belonging to another key.
methods.name: deployment/api-keys/put

methods.description: Returns non-secret key metadata, all keys or those of one scope, including groups, revocation and last-use timestamps. Plaintext secrets are never stored or returned.
methods.name: deployment/api-keys/list

methods.description: Atomically replaces an active key's secret with a generated one, immediately rejecting the old secret on subsequent requests. Preserves the key id, scope, groups, actor authority, name, creator and creation time; clears last use. Returns the new secret once. An unknown or revoked key is not found. Already admitted work continues.
methods.name: deployment/api-keys/rotate

methods.description: Revokes the key of this id and scope; revoking a revoked key keeps its first revocation time. An unknown key is not found. A revoked key keeps its key id.
methods.name: deployment/api-keys/revoke

methods.description: Registers or replaces a deployment provider: controller endpoint, optional data route base, and optional bearer credential for controller and data routes (write-only: kept when omitted, removed by clearCredential, never returned). The controller is probed: a definitive refusal is invalidRequest, unreachable is accepted. The provider never calls Lightspeed.
methods.name: deployment/environment-providers/put

methods.description: Returns every deployment-registered provider with its controller endpoint, data route base, and whether a credential is stored.
methods.name: deployment/environment-providers/list

methods.description: Returns one deployment-registered provider with its controller endpoint, data route base, and whether a credential is stored.
methods.name: deployment/environment-providers/read

methods.description: Deletes a deployment provider only when no universe binding and no non-closed environment references it.
methods.name: deployment/environment-providers/delete

methods.description: Creates or replaces one universe's binding to a deployment provider. Only an enabled binding admits creates, template listing, and data routes for the universe.
methods.name: deployment/environment-providers/bindings/put

methods.description: Deletes a universe's binding to a provider only when the universe has no non-closed environment of that provider.
methods.name: deployment/environment-providers/bindings/delete

methods.description: The connector host's discovery call: every enabled provider account of the deployment with its universe id and credential grant reference. Re-poll to pick up accounts created or disabled since.
methods.name: deployment/channels/accounts/list
